statement: The published decay hybrid reports 99.8% temporal accuracy on its own benchmark, which shows decay-based ranking can be near-ceiling when the temporally correct evidence is also the recent evidence, but it does not show decay is sufficient when the in-force version is old: the discriminating case (an old in-force clause coexisting with a recent near-duplicate version of the same clause) is not isolated by that figure, and the metric's definition is not verifiable from the accessible record. The decisive test for whether recency is a sufficient proxy is therefore restricted to non-latest-authoritative queries, where decay and valid-time gating make opposite predictions by construction.
